h1: Video production, animation and AI video for Houston companies
intro: 22 Signals makes video production Houston companies use to sell, train and recruit: brand films, short-form reels, motion graphics, 2D and 3D animation and clearly labeled AI video. We are strongest where a product or process is hard to film, such as plant equipment, a medical procedure or a spacecraft part, and animation explains it better.

p: A lot of what Houston companies sell cannot simply be pointed at with a camera. A downhole tool works two miles underground. A catalyst does its job inside a reactor. A heart device sits inside a patient. A life-support component is built for a spacecraft most people will never see. Filming the factory floor shows none of it.

That is why animation is so useful here. A clear 3D sequence of a tool string or a valve opening can do more for a sales team at a trade booth than any brochure. A procedure animation helps a surgeon explain options to a patient. A motion graphics explainer turns a dense engineering process into ninety seconds a buyer will actually watch.

sections.h: Training and safety video that crews will watch
p: Plants and contractors along the Ship Channel and across Greater Houston run constant training: site orientation, lockout and tagout, confined space, hazard communication. Most of the existing videos are long, dated and in English only. We make shorter modules, built around the real site where possible, and in Spanish as well as English. We work with your safety team on every script, because a training video that gets a procedure slightly wrong is worse than none.

AI video can cut the cost of some work sharply: ad variations for testing, a presenter who can deliver the same message in several languages, or generated backgrounds for scenes that would be costly to shoot. We use it where it fits and label it clearly. A person reviews every frame before it goes out. We do not use AI to fake real people, places or results, and we avoid it for medical or safety content where accuracy must be checked shot by shot.

sections.h: Getting more from every shoot day
p: Shoot days are the costly part of video production. Houston traffic alone can eat half a day moving a crew from a Pasadena plant to an office in the Energy Corridor. So we plan each shoot to feed months of content: one long brand film, a set of short cut-downs for LinkedIn and Instagram, stills for the website, interview clips for recruiting and b-roll for future ads. Planned that way, a single day of video production gives Houston marketing teams a library rather than one finished asset.

We run a managed video editing team for a US client, turning raw footage into finished posts and ads every week. It is the model we offer Houston companies that need a steady flow of content: a set team, a style guide, a review process and agreed turnaround times.

list: Talk: what the video must achieve, who will watch it and where.
Plan: script, storyboard, style frames and schedule, with dates in writing.
Build: shoot, animation and edit, with review rounds agreed up front.

With a six-hour gap, edits requested in your afternoon are often in your inbox the next morning. Live-action shoots in Houston are arranged when the project needs them, using crews we brief and direct. For live broadcast, we bring the experience of more than 20 large-scale live events run and broadcast, where the date never moves. Your Signal Lead is accountable for every deliverable.

faqs.a: Yes, when the project needs live footage. We plan and direct the shoot and work with camera crews on the ground, while editing and animation happen remotely. Many Houston projects, such as technical or medical animation, need no shoot at all, which keeps them quicker to produce and easier to update later.

faqs.q: Can you animate equipment from our CAD files?
faqs.a: Yes. We can import models from common CAD formats, simplify them for animation and show internal parts or movement accurately. This is common for oilfield and process equipment makers in Houston. If you need to protect proprietary details, we can simplify or hide parts before anything is shown publicly.

faqs.q: Do you make medical animations for hospitals and device companies?
faqs.a: Yes. We create procedure, mechanism-of-action and patient education animations. Every script and frame is reviewed by your clinical and regulatory teams before release, and we keep claims within what your approvals allow. Texas Medical Center institutions and device makers often need content for patients, sales teams and conferences from the same project.

faqs.q: Can you produce safety training videos in Spanish?
faqs.a: Yes. We produce training in English and Spanish, with scripts reviewed by your safety team and voiceover by native speakers. Shorter modules usually work better than one long video, and they are easier to update when a procedure changes. We can also add captions for noisy environments.

faqs.q: Is AI video right for our company?
faqs.a: It suits some jobs well, such as ad variations, multilingual presenter videos and generated backgrounds. It is a poor fit for safety, medical or technical content where every detail must be exactly right. We always label AI video and have a person review it, and we will tell you when traditional production is the better choice.

faqs.q: How long does a video take?
faqs.a: For video production, Houston clients find a short social video is the quickest job, while a brand film or a detailed 3D animation takes longer, depending on reviews and shoots. We agree the schedule and review rounds in writing at the start, so you know when each draft will arrive.
